ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Consider the following simple model of a bow and arrow. An ideal elastic string has a spring constant $k=10 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}$ and relaxed length $L=1 \mathrm{~m}$ which is attached to the ends of an inflexible fixed steel rod of the same length $L$ as shown below. A small ball of mass $m=2 \mathrm{~kg}$ and the thread are pulled by its midpoint away from the rod until each individual part of the thread have the same length of the rod, as shown below. What is the speed of the ball in meters per seconds right after it stops accelerating? Assume the whole setup is carried out in zero gravity.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a fixed vertical rod on the left labeled L. An elastic string is attached to the top and bottom ends of the rod and is pulled to the right at its midpoint, where a small ball labeled m is located. The two slanted string segments from the rod ends to the ball are each labeled L. Reasoning: The elastic string is treated as one ideal spring with spring constant k = 10 N/m and relaxed total length L = 1 m. In the pulled configuration, each half of the string has length L, so the total string length is 2L. Therefore the extension of the whole string is 2L - L = L. The initial elastic potential energy is (1/2)kL^2. The ball stops accelerating when the string returns to its relaxed total length L, so the spring force becomes zero. With zero gravity and no losses, this spring energy becomes the kinetic energy of the ball: (1/2)kL^2 = (1/2)mv^2. Thus v = L sqrt(k/m) = 1 * sqrt(10/2) = sqrt(5) ≈ 2.23 m/s.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: the image shows symmetric upper and lower string segments from the top and bottom of a vertical rod to the ball at the right, so the ball moves along the perpendicular bisector of the rod. Let x be the horizontal distance from the rod midpoint to the ball. From the image and text, the fixed endpoints are separated by L, so each instantaneous half-string length is ell = sqrt(x^2 + (L/2)^2). The initially drawn state has each half-string length L, hence x_i = sqrt(L^2 - (L/2)^2) = (sqrt(3)/2)L. The total string length is 2ell, so the tension is T = k(2ell - L). The horizontal spring force on the ball is F = 2T(x/ell). The acceleration stops at x = 0, where ell = L/2 and the total string length is the relaxed length L. Compute the work done by the string: W = integral from 0 to x_i of 2k(2ell - L)(x/ell) dx. With u = 2ell - L, du = 2x/ell dx, so W = integral from 0 to L of k u du = 1/2 kL^2. Set W = 1/2 mv^2 to get v = sqrt(kL^2/m) = sqrt(5) ≈ 2.23 m/s.

图像描述：附图中左侧是一根竖直固定钢杆，标为长度 L；钢杆的上下两端分别连接两段斜向右方的弹性弦，两段弦在右侧相交于小球 m。两段斜弦都标为 L，且图形关于钢杆中点的水平线对称，所以小球沿钢杆的垂直平分线运动。

推理：令小球到钢杆中点的水平距离为 x。由于钢杆两端间距为 L，每段半弦的瞬时长度为 ell = sqrt(x^2 + (L/2)^2)。初始拉开时每一段弦长都等于 L，因此 x_i = sqrt(L^2 - (L/2)^2) = (sqrt(3)/2)L。整根弦的总长度为 2ell，弦的松弛长度为 L，所以张力 T = k(2ell - L)。两段弦的竖直分力相互抵消，水平合力大小为 F = 2T(x/ell) = 2k(2ell - L)(x/ell)。当小球到达 x = 0 时，ell = L/2，总弦长 2ell = L，弦恢复松弛长度，张力为 0，因此加速度停止。

弦对小球做的功为 W = integral from 0 to x_i of 2k(2ell - L)(x/ell) dx。令 u = 2ell - L，则 du = 2x/ell dx，所以 W = integral from 0 to L of k u du = (1/2)kL^2。由能量守恒，(1/2)mv^2 = (1/2)kL^2，因此 v = sqrt(kL^2/m)。代入 k = 10 N/m、L = 1 m、m = 2 kg，v = sqrt(10/2) = sqrt(5) ≈ 2.23 m/s。
